purpose.public_purpose: Help adults discover and book small in-person craft workshops without feeling overwhelmed by a course marketplace.
purpose.primary_outcome: A visitor finds a suitable workshop and completes a booking request.
success_signals: Visitors can compare upcoming workshops by date, skill level, and available places
The booking path is understandable without account creation
The full primary journey remains usable by keyboard and at 320 CSS pixels
trust_requirements: Show real instructors and venue details
State price, materials, accessibility, cancellation, and duration before booking

audience.primary: Adults interested in trying a practical craft workshop locally
audience.context_of_use: Browsing on a phone after seeing a social post or searching for a weekend activity
risks: Overly artistic layout hiding practical details
Mobile booking controls obscured by sticky elements

surfaces.purpose: Explain the workshop concept and route visitors to suitable upcoming sessions.
Let visitors compare current sessions without losing important practical information.
Provide every decision detail and start a booking request.

primary_journeys: Social or search entry → upcoming workshop scan → detail → booking request → confirmation
Home → how it works → workshop list → detail
experience_map.completion_path: A booking or waitlist request returns a visible confirmation, sends an email receipt, and offers a clear next step.
experience_map.navigation_model: Simple top-level navigation with Home, Workshops, How it works, and Visit; workshop detail preserves a clear return to the filtered list.

visual_grammar.dominant_idea: A contemporary workshop noticeboard combining tactile paper detail with clear editorial scheduling.
typography_roles: Warm display serif for workshop names
Highly legible sans serif for schedules, forms, and practical details
Tabular numerals for dates, duration, price, and places
colour_roles: Deep green action and focus colour
Clay accent reserved for dates and availability
Semantic status colours with text labels
layout_rules: Date and availability remain visually adjacent
Practical details appear before long editorial description
Artwork may overlap frames but never booking controls
Desktop uses asymmetric editorial columns; narrow screens use a direct single-column decision order
visual_grammar.spacing_density: Airy around editorial imagery, compact and regular around schedule and booking information.
visual_grammar.imagery_treatment: Real workshop process photography with natural crop, visible materials, and no artificial yellow grading.
component_language: Workshop cards behave as schedule entries rather than generic floating cards
Filters use native controls with explicit applied-state summary
Booking appears in a focused dialog on wide screens and a full route or full-height sheet on narrow screens

project_drivers: Visitors must compare date, availability, price and level before committing attention to editorial description.
The workshops are physical making experiences, so real materials, hands and process are more trustworthy than generic classroom imagery.
Booking confidence depends on practical clarity rather than luxury or technology spectacle.

mechanisms.mechanism: Treat workshop discovery as an editorial noticeboard whose strongest visual units are date, availability and the object being made rather than a generic course-card grid.
mechanisms.project_reason: The primary user decision is schedule-and-fit comparison, while the craft context benefits from tactile editorial framing.
must_not_become: A decorative collage that obscures dates or actions
A repeated floating-card layout with editorial styling applied only as surface decoration

mechanisms.mechanism: Use real making-process imagery as trust evidence and visual punctuation around practical information.
mechanisms.project_reason: Visible tools, hands and materials prove the physical nature of the workshop more credibly than stock lifestyle photography.
must_not_become: Atmospheric imagery that pushes practical details below the fold
A generated craft aesthetic presented as documentary evidence

category_contrasts: Avoid presenting every workshop as an interchangeable online-course tile.
Avoid false urgency and growth-marketing language; availability should read as practical information.
familiar_patterns_kept: Keep conventional top-level navigation because orientation is more valuable than novel navigation here.
Keep native or semantically standard form controls for filters and booking.
Keep dates, prices, availability and error states explicit rather than turning them into visual metaphors.
anti_repetition_rules: Do not inherit a previous SITECRAFT project's hero composition, recurring motif, chapter sequence or signature transition unless this workshop brief independently justifies it.
Do not add motion, 3D, generated video or unusual navigation merely to make the site feel more premium.

direction_selection.reason: The workshop brief already establishes a clear content-first editorial scheduling direction, so manufacturing alternative concepts would add ceremony rather than improve the experience.
reopen_conditions: The project owner rejects the approved editorial scheduling direction.
New user or content evidence shows that the current structure does not support workshop comparison or booking confidence.

interaction_rules: Filtering updates the result summary and URL without moving keyboard focus unexpectedly
Booking state is recoverable after validation errors
Availability is always expressed with text, not colour alone
transition_grammar: Workshop thumbnail may transition into the detail hero as progressive enhancement
Filter changes use a short local cross-fade without moving the page
Dialog entry is a restrained opacity and vertical offset
scroll_rules: Sticky booking summary is disabled when viewport height is constrained
motion_purposes: Preserve continuity from list to detail
Confirm filtering and booking state changes
reduced_motion: Remove shared-element travel and use an immediate route change
Replace dialog travel with an immediate opacity change
Keep focus movement and status announcements unchanged
focus_behaviour: Detail route focus moves to the workshop heading after navigation
Booking dialog receives focus on its heading and returns focus to the invoking button on close
Validation errors focus the summary, with linked fields
loading_error_feedback: Errors explain what failed and provide retry
Booking submission prevents duplicate requests while retaining entered values

preserve: Warm paper / charcoal / deep-green visual family
Making-process imagery remains documentary rather than decorative

state_dimensions.authority: The URL, selected workshop record and booking state own the current experience state; motion and imagery may reflect it but may not invent a different state.

family_checks: Review Home, workshop list and workshop detail together to confirm they feel like one workshop service rather than three independently styled pages.
stale_conditions: A page or generated asset is stale if it preserves the visual brand but depicts or implies a workshop, availability, booking, or route state that is no longer authoritative.

notes: Documentary source media; generated campaign assets must never be represented as descendants of this evidence asset.
Approved still master and protected identity anchor for later motion/video branches.
Static and reduced-motion fallback derived directly from the approved key art.
Lightweight authored motion branch; not the same artifact as the generated video branch.
Generated video master must preserve the approved key-art identity and remain separate from the web-delivery derivative.
Compressed website derivative; acceptance depends on the generated master and real-page delivery evidence.

rules: parent_asset_ids mean direct derivation; reference_asset_ids mean influence without direct derivation.
Every consequential image/video/motion asset named by the contract must use the same stable asset ID in the lineage spine and asset ledger.
Delivered derivatives retain their own IDs so approval and performance evidence cannot be confused with the source master.

asset_roles.purpose: Show real materials, instructors, and making activity so visitors can judge the experience accurately.
asset_roles.subject: Owner-approved real workshop process photography.
asset_roles.focal_rule: Keep hands, tools, and the making action intact; do not crop to generic smiling portraits.
asset_roles.text_relationship: Practical details remain in HTML beside the image rather than embedded in it.

asset_roles.surface: Rare campaign entry moment and social preview
asset_roles.purpose: Extend the tactile noticeboard identity with one original paper-form motif without pretending it is documentary workshop evidence.
asset_roles.subject: An abstract folded-paper programme mark built from simple original shapes.
asset_roles.focal_rule: The complete mark remains recognisable at small sizes and preserves a clean text-free zone.
asset_roles.text_relationship: Website copy remains semantic DOM text; social-preview text is added in the layout tool from approved copy.

reference_roles.contribution: Preserve the real venue, materials, instructors, and making actions.
reference_roles.rights_status: Owner-supplied and approved for this example contract.

reference_roles.contribution: Inform asymmetrical framing and the relationship between image, date, and practical information.
reference_roles.rights_status: Mechanism-only internal study; not publishable as an asset.

reference_roles.contribution: Inform warm paper, clay, charcoal, and deep-green material relationships for the generated programme mark.

production_stages: Map every image to a named surface and user-facing purpose.
Approve documentary photography separately from generated campaign assets.
Generate and approve the still programme-mark master before motion.
Prepare responsive and social derivatives with explicit crop rules.
Integrate and observe the assets in wide, short-laptop, narrow, and reduced-motion states.

generation_routes.capability_class: Graphic and vector-system output with strong instruction and edit fidelity
generation_routes.selected_route: Provider-neutral image or illustration workflow selected at production time
generation_routes.reason: The asset needs original simple geometry, material control, a text-free master, and reliable derivative creation.
generation_routes.fallback: Human-built SVG or layered design-tool composition using the same approved brief.
limitations: No provider is assumed to remain permanently best
Generated geometry must be inspected and may require manual cleanup

execution_policy.iteration_rule: Repair one diagnosed defect at a time and repeat protected invariants on every edit iteration.
execution_policy.host_reference_rule: A local path is not automatically an image-model input; the executing host must confirm each required reference is actually available to the generator before the job is ready.

production_jobs.acceptance_gate: The programme mark must preserve the approved visual brief, remain text-free, read clearly at small size, and pass full-resolution inspection before any dependent derivative or motion work begins.
notes: This is a generation job using bounded references, not an edit of either reference image.

preservation_rules: Generated assets must never alter or fabricate documentary workshop evidence.
The approved programme-mark silhouette, paper palette, and text-free master are protected after approval.
Important typography is added outside the generated image.
derivative_rules: Use art-directed wide and narrow crops when the making action changes by aspect ratio.
Declare intrinsic dimensions and focal guidance for every derivative.
Keep a square text-free programme-mark master for future repair.
motion_handoff: Motion begins only from the approved programme-mark still master.
The handoff names protected geometry, palette, poster frame, stable end state, reduced-motion frame, and prohibited deformation.
A motion reference may control timing or folding behaviour only; it may not replace the mark's design.
delivery: Serve responsive workshop photography with picture/srcset and declared dimensions.
Deliver the generated programme mark as the lightest maintainable format that preserves the approved appearance.
Provide static poster and social-preview derivatives.
accessibility: Documentary images receive concise purpose-led alt text.
The programme mark is decorative unless it communicates programme identity not already present in text.
No essential copy is embedded only in an image.
performance: Do not lazy-load the actual LCP workshop image.
Bound image dimensions and compression by surface.
Animated derivatives must not cause layout shift or continuous offscreen work.
lineage: Record source, rights, prompt or edit instruction, references, model or human route, date, checksum, derivatives, owner, and approval state in the asset ledger.
evidence: Wide, short-laptop, narrow, 320 CSS-pixel, social-preview, and reduced-motion captures
LCP, CLS, crop, alt-text, rights, and owner-approval review

asset_roles.purpose: Give the generated programme identity a short tactile paper-fold motion moment without implying documentary workshop footage.
asset_roles.first_frame_requirement: Begin on the approved programme-mark silhouette in a stable poster-compatible state so failed autoplay, poster display, and the generated clip describe the same identity.
asset_roles.last_frame_requirement: Return to the same approved silhouette, framing, material state, and visual weight closely enough to create a clean loop and a stable handoff back to the static fallback.
continuity_requirements: Preserve the approved programme-mark silhouette, paper material, palette, and centre-weighted crop throughout the clip.
Do not introduce a different workshop, booking state, logo, text, or documentary-looking footage while the generated identity loop is playing.
copy_crop_rules: Keep the mark in the centre 60 percent so wide and narrow derivatives remain usable
Do not place essential text inside the generated video

reference_roles.contribution: Controls the exact approved mark silhouette, paper material and palette.
ignore: Any accidental background or presentation framing from the reference export
reference_roles.rights_status: Project-owned generated campaign asset approved for this example

generation_policy.provider_strategy: Choose an authenticated video generator that can preserve the approved mark, produce a short controlled loop, return an inspectable artifact, and support bounded regeneration.
generation_policy.approval_boundary: Provider inspection is authorized separately from generation. After inspection, the example authorizes at most three generation attempts and 120 provider credits; increasing either requires owner approval.
stop_conditions: Stop when 120 reported provider credits are reached
Stop when the provider-interaction budget is exhausted
Stop after two attempts fail the same hard floor without material improvement
Stop if the approved mark would need to be redesigned rather than animated

hard_floors: Approved programme-mark silhouette remains recognizable and stable
No unwanted text, watermark or logo artifact
quality_gate.acceptance_rule: Accept only when every hard floor passes on the actual generated artifact; a strong average impression cannot override identity drift or a broken loop.
quality_gate.regeneration_rule: Change only the diagnosed failing prompt, reference-role or generation setting while preserving dimensions that already passed.

delivery: Create a compressed web derivative and poster rather than shipping the generation master directly
Verify the loop inside the real home composition before approval
accessibility: Treat the loop as non-essential identity media
Use the static approved programme mark for reduced motion and failed media loading
performance: Do not preload the loop when it is not the LCP candidate
Pause or avoid continuous offscreen playback
Keep the delivered video within the page media budget
lineage: Record provider/model/tool when known, prompt/reference revision, attempt ID, reported credits, artifact hash, review decision and accepted derivative lineage

continuity_devices: Shared workshop imagery and quiet paper-texture treatment maintain orientation without forcing a recurring motif.
roles: Interface feedback for filtering and booking
Continuity between workshop list and detail
A restrained animated programme mark for rare campaign moments
motion_system.emotional_temperature: Tactile, calm, human, and quietly celebratory rather than energetic or theatrical.
narrative_beats: Settle into a static, fully readable end frame

duration_roles: 150–240 ms for filters and compact disclosure
One 500–650 ms expressive programme-mark sequence used only at rare entry moments
easing_roles: Use standard easing when an element remains visible throughout
sequence_rules: Practical information is readable before decorative motion begins
No more than two coordinated moving groups
The important content finishes in the stable end frame
spatial_rules: Shared workshop imagery preserves identity between list and detail
Direction may distinguish forward and back navigation
loop_rules: The programme mark plays once and does not loop
No ambient motion continues while the visitor reads booking information

kinetic_typography: Workshop names remain semantic DOM text
No essential copy is revealed character by character
Animated type settles before the primary action becomes the focal point
compositing_rules: Transparent edges are reviewed on warm paper and charcoal backgrounds
Texture and motion blur remain subtle and do not reduce legibility

delivery_routes.reason: Preserve identity between a selected workshop and its detail while keeping navigation progressive.
delivery_routes.runtime: Browser View Transition API when supported
delivery_routes.fallback: Immediate navigation with focus moved to the detail heading.
budget: No route is blocked by transition failure

delivery_routes.reason: The mark uses a small number of scalable paper shapes and simple masks.
delivery_routes.runtime: CSS keyframes with no external library

playback_rules: Motion begins only after the relevant asset is ready
accessibility_equivalents: Reduced motion removes shared-element travel and shows the stable end frame
The programme mark is decorative and has a static equivalent
Focus movement and status announcements remain unchanged
performance_budget: No continuous frame callback remains active after settling
Input responsiveness is measured while motion is active
ownership: The Experience Contract owns motion intent and evidence
The approved asset ledger owns source, rights, and revision
Implementation owns runtime integration and fallback
evidence: Storyboard and style frame for the programme mark
Wide, short-laptop, narrow, and reduced-motion recordings
Start, key beat, and settled-state screenshots
Frame pacing and input responsiveness review

compositions.name: wide editorial
compositions.trigger: The main content container can support imagery and decision information side by side.
layout_changes: Keep booking summary visible in the secondary column
interaction_changes: Booking opens in a modal dialog

compositions.name: short laptop
compositions.trigger: Viewport height is too small for a persistent secondary booking column.
layout_changes: Keep action inline after practical details
interaction_changes: Dialog height is bounded with internal content scrolling only when necessary

compositions.name: narrow
compositions.trigger: Available inline size no longer supports two decision columns.
layout_changes: Place availability and primary action before the long description
Use full-width media with approved crop
interaction_changes: Booking becomes a dedicated route or full-height sheet
content_priority_changes: Practical details move before instructor biography

reflow_320_css_px: Sticky controls do not obscure focused content
intrinsic_media_rules: All workshop images declare intrinsic dimensions
Use art-directed sources where the focal making action differs by crop

implementation.architecture: Server-rendered content site with progressively enhanced filtering and booking interactions.
conventions: Semantic HTML and native controls first
Design tokens own colour, type, spacing, and focus
Booking and catalogue state have explicit loading and error models
editable_areas: Component details within the visual grammar
Motion timing within the declared ranges

capability_plan.need: Preserve orientation when moving between workshop list and detail without making navigation dependent on animation.
capability_plan.selected_route: Browser-native View Transition API as progressive enhancement where supported.
capability_plan.reason: The platform feature can provide shared visual continuity while ordinary document navigation remains the authoritative route behaviour.
rejected_routes: Convert the public programme into a client-only SPA solely to obtain animated route transitions.
Add a general animation framework only for this one navigation effect.
integration_boundary: The routing layer owns URLs, history, loading and focus.
The transition layer may animate approved visual continuity but may not own navigation state.
loading_strategy: No additional transition runtime is loaded; unsupported browsers use ordinary navigation.
capability_plan.fallback: Normal navigation with the same semantic destination, focus movement and content.
risks: Cross-browser rendering differences must not affect navigation or focus.
Reduced motion must remove travel without removing orientation.
evidence_required: Normal and reduced-motion list-to-detail navigation recording.
Environment-scoped fallback evidence in a browser without the enhanced transition.

capability_plan.need: Provide fast filtering and recoverable booking interaction while keeping the public programme readable and useful before client enhancement.
capability_plan.selected_route: Small progressively enhanced client state inside the existing project architecture.
capability_plan.reason: The interaction needs local state and immediate feedback, but does not justify replacing server-rendered public content or introducing a second application architecture.
rejected_routes: Introduce a second state-management runtime for the bounded filter and booking state.
integration_boundary: Server-rendered content remains the content authority.
Client state owns only active filters, local booking interaction state and status feedback.
URLs remain shareable and browser history remains meaningful.
loading_strategy: Enhancement initializes after semantic controls and programme content are available.
capability_plan.fallback: Server routes and native form behaviour preserve the core programme and booking path when enhancement is unavailable.
risks: Client and server filter state can drift if URL ownership is unclear.
Loading and validation feedback must remain accessible.
evidence_required: Filter, empty-state, back-navigation and URL-state checks.
Booking validation and recovery keyboard run.
Input-responsiveness observation for filter and booking actions.

ownership.rule: URLs, browser history, loading and focus remain authoritative in normal navigation; the visual transition may observe the route change but may not replace it.

ownership.scope: Workshop filters and local booking interaction
ownership.rule: Client state owns only active filters and local booking interaction state; public programme content remains server-authoritative.

ownership.scope: Public routes, filters and booking controls
ownership.owner: Semantic DOM and native control layer
ownership.rule: Transitions and client state must preserve native focus order, visible focus and keyboard completion paths.

bridges.mechanism: Progressive-enhancement handoff after an approved navigation change
bridges.contract: Navigation commits the destination and focus semantics; the transition layer only supplies visual continuity when supported.
Client filter changes update the approved URL representation without creating a second routing authority.

shared_rules: The Experience Contract and design tokens remain the visual authority across every runtime.
Native scrolling, semantic reading order and browser history remain intact.
Reduced-motion behaviour is coordinated across transitions and local client enhancement rather than implemented independently by each layer.
prohibited_conflicts: No second route manager may be introduced solely for animation.
No second client-state runtime may own the same filter or booking state.
No transition layer may move keyboard focus independently of the semantic navigation result.

browser_support: Full function without View Transition API
public_private_boundary: Private attendee details remain server-side and are not embedded in public pages
Internal capacity notes are excluded from public API responses
implementation.rollback_boundary: Each implementation batch must be reversible without replacing approved photography or catalogue data.

required_views: 320 CSS-pixel reflow for home, list, detail, and booking
required_interactions: Keyboard navigation from home to booking confirmation
Filter apply, clear, and empty result
Dialog or sheet open, close, escape, and focus return
accessibility_checks: Zoom, text spacing, and 320 CSS-pixel reflow
performance_checks: LCP resource and hero image review
CLS during image, filter, and availability loading
INP for filters and booking submission
security_checks: Public bundle and API response inspection
Direct access and authorization review for private booking data

limitations: No environment evidence has been collected for this buildable example.
The exact managed browser and assistive technology must be selected from the deployment context.
This row is required only if Linux desktop support remains in the approved browser promise.

evidence_contract.support_claim_rule: Current evergreen browser support is not verified until every material environment row is passed, marked not required, or explicitly accepted as a bounded exclusion by the owner.
evidence_contract.freshness_rule: Any change to layout, content priority, booking behaviour, protected imagery, responsive rules, browser support, or platform-specific behaviour stales the affected evidence rows.

revision_history.summary: Initial buildable contract for the example workshop booking experience.
